lokeśaḥ karaṇāni yasya mahimā taṃ netranāthaṃ stumaḥ	 || 1 ||
translation: The Lord of the world, whose majesty [extends to] the sense-organs — him, the Lord Netra, we praise.
I praise the Netra, whose essence is the fivefold and sevenfold — the gracious one, the single hero of the two Śivas.

sanskrit: bodhollāso jayati sa guruḥ ko'pyapūrvo rahasyaḥ	|| 3 ||
translation: That guru — the joy of awakening — triumphs: a certain unprecedented one, [keeper] of the secret.
The Śaiva Netra shines forth here and in the hereafter, for the grace of the world.
Taste, O sapid ones, [this] fragrance — for the stilling of the vāsanās of the world, [which is] fragrant but essenceless.
The arising, abiding, and dissolution of the whole universe [come about] through śakti.
To Śiva, the supreme Self, [who is] supreme over Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Īśa.
Consciousness is declared in all treatises to be the form of the Self.
The fashioning of the Three-eyed One is shown to me here for that purpose.

sanskrit: krīḍamānaṃ gaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ pārvatyā sahitaṃ haram || 1-3 ||
translation: Hara, sporting with the gaṇas, together with Pārvatī.
Pārvatī, having quickly descended from his lap, grasped [his] two feet.
O Blessed One, O Lord of the gods' God, O world-lord, O master of the universe —

sanskrit: sarvasya jagato deva kintu me parameśvara || 1-6 ||
translation: O God, O Supreme Lord — [you belong] to the whole world, but [you are] mine.

sanskrit: kārtikeyasya ca na me na sureṣu gaṇeṣu vā || 1-7 ||
translation: Not in Kārtikeya, nor in me, nor among the gods, nor among the hosts [of gaṇas], nor anywhere else.

sanskrit: tadadya me jagannātha prasanno'si yadi prabho || 1-8 ||
translation: If now, O Lord of the world, O Lord, you are gracious to me —
I entreat [you]: you are worthy to tell me, who have taken refuge [in you], this in its entirety.
Having thus heard the Goddess's speech, his face breaking into a smile, he spoke.
The treatise has issued forth.
[The treatise that issued] of which the mouth [spoke] — fragmentary.
Gratified by you, O sinless one, I shall tell everything without doubt.
In the reading, the meaning is clear.
Never was such a delightful wonder heard; that [now] I hear.
O Blessed One, [it] is to be told by you to me without envy.
I hear that ascertained truth; I wish to master it.
How did that terrible fire arise from him — the burner of Kāla [Time/Death]?
O God, why was that terrible deed done, [springing] from the desire to burn Fire and Kāla?
And Kāma likewise, O Supreme Lord, was burnt up in play.
Which deed, done by the God of gods, causes great wonder.

sanskrit: kiṃ vā vahnimayaṃ cakṣustatkathaṃ na vibhāvyate	|| 1-17 ||
translation: Or what — an eye made of fire; how is that not conceived?
With [that] wholly made of nectar you nourish the world in a moment.
Bright like the form of nectar, [the eye] that causes the world's nourishment.
O Blessed One, you ought to tell all this in brief.
'Born' — this appears contradictory; establish it, O Supreme Lord, [I pray].
That which [is] in the interior of my eye — the fire; or that unsurpassed nectar —
The relation is indeed well known as sixfold.
Whose own form is innate, pure, all-pervading, facing in all directions.
Attainable through yoga, difficult to approach, hard to obtain for those whose selves are unrefined.
That is the power of all powers; that indeed is the strength of the strong.

sanskrit: sā mamecchā parā śaktiḥ śaktiyuktā svabhāvajā || 1-25 ||
translation: She is my supreme Will — the śakti, joined with śakti, born of [my] own nature.

sanskrit: sarvasya jagato vāpi svā śaktiḥ kāraṇātmikā || 1-26 ||
translation: Of the whole world too, she is the own śakti, whose essence is causality.
She indeed is the Will, having the form of knowledge, and extended through the qualities beginning with action.

sanskrit: sā vai mahākriyārūpā saṃsthitaikā kriyā matā	|| 1-28 ||
translation: She indeed, whose form is the Great Action, abiding as one, is held to be Action.
Thus my Will is called the śakti, [variously] named 'knowledge' and named 'action.'
The fashioning of the Three-eyed One is shown to me here for that purpose.
Vimarśa — reflexive awareness — is the supreme śakti, all-knowing, possessed of gnosis.
'Light,' so it is declared by the good — [yet it is] perception, lusterless.

sanskrit: icchātvaṃ tasya sā devī sisṛkṣoḥ pratipadyate	||" (mā. vi. 3-5)
translation: She, the Goddess, becomes the will-state of him who desires to create.
Making [all] know, here in the world, she is called the knowledge-śakti.

sanskrit: jātā tadaiva tattadvat kurvatyatra kriyocyate ||" (mā. vi. 3-8)
translation: Arising then indeed, doing this and that here, she is called Action.
[…] blazes forth — the action-śakti, in the form of the moon. (fragmentary)
But then the Three-eyed One is to be known [thus].

sanskrit: ca sṛṣṭiṃ sthitiṃ saṃhṛtiṃ ca tritanurvidadhāmyaham	|| 1-31 ||
translation: And creation, abiding, and dissolution — I, whose body is the triad, perform.
Those who say the Blessed Lord has agency in creation and so on are deluded, indeed.
The unsurpassed nectar of the Netra, whose form is Will, Knowledge, and Action.
Such is called unsurpassed.
That which is supreme bliss, this which is the supreme abode —
Declared by the Conqueror of Death, it grants liberation to all.
By which, indeed, through mere recollection, they are freed.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhṛti mukto'sau na punarjanma cāpnuyāt ||" (ne. 8-9)
translation: From then on he is freed; he would not undergo rebirth again.
[It is] freedom from touching future suffering, granting release from all suffering.
[We worship] the God who removes all diseases, the auspicious Śiva who removes all ailments.
